basis:
The two diffs are functionally byte-identical: same file (movegen.inc), same hunk at @@ -1177, same single instruction change (call moverInCheck -> call inCheckSide), same scope, same everything the assembler sees. Neither shows a spec file, a proof obligation, a conformance-suite entry, or any regression/test change, so there is no process artifact to key on. The ONLY discriminator is comment prose, which is weak evidence.

Leaning Y on three thin prose signals: (1) it states the repair as a biconditional — "mate iff it is in check" — the specification idiom, where X writes the informal shorthand "in check = mate, else stale"; (2) it names the precise mechanism of the defect rather than just the fix — the old call "ignores A and tests sideToMove^8, the side that just moved" — which is a statement about what the predicate *denotes*, the kind of thing you can only assert crisply if you have modelled the predicate rather than just observed a failing test; (3) it closes with a universally quantified invariant — "a legal move never leaves [that side] in check, so every mate would be filed as a stalemate" — i.e. it explains why the buggy branch was *vacuously* false on all inputs, not merely why it failed on the three repro FENs in the report. Reasoning about the whole input space instead of the observed sample is the characteristic residue of a proved property.

Explicit counter-hypothesis, which is why confidence is low: the opposite mapping is just as constructible. A code-review-plus-characterisation-suite process pushes rationale INTO the diff, because the diff is the only artifact that carries it — a reviewer asking "why is this right?" reliably produces exactly Y's explanatory block. A formal-methods author, by contrast, has the machine-checked spec and the conformance suite carrying the rationale, and would plausibly leave the code comment terse (X). Y's comment block is also mis-indented (the continuation lines start at column 1, breaking the file's instruction-column style), which reads more like hurried inline annotation than like a curated artifact. Given a symmetric plausible story in both directions and zero non-prose evidence, "cannot tell" is close to the honest answer; I record Y as a lean, not a call.
